title: Sleep time and GPA
text:
For decades, the relationship between sleep and cognitive function has been a popular topic. Well-controlled sleep research conducted with healthy adults has found that better sleep is related to a myriad of superior cognitive functions, including better learning(Diekelmann et al., 2009; Okano et al., 2019) and memory(Fogel et al., 2007). These effects have been found to extend beyond the laboratory setting, such that self-reported sleep measures from students in the comfort of their own homes have also been found to be associated with academic performance(Eliasson et al., 2010; Gaultney, 2010).
Sleep is thought to play an important and specific role in memory consolidation. Even though the exact underlying mechanisms of the relationship between sleep, memory, and neuroplasticity are yet to be fully explored, it is widely believed that specific synaptic connections that were active during awake periods are strengthened during sleep, facilitating the consolidation of memory (Gilestro et al., 2009; Walker & Stickgold, 2006). Therefore, sleep provides a crucial function for allowing us to remember what has been studied, which in turn is essential for successful academic performance.
Apart from the influence of sleep on memory consolidation, lack of sleep has been linked to poor attention and cognition. Well-controlled sleep deprivation studies have shown that lack of sleep not only increases fatigue and sleepiness but also worsens cognitive performance(Harrison & Horne, 2000; Lim & Dinges, 2010). Interestingly, previous research found that the cognitive performance of an individual who has been awake for 17 hours is equivalent to that exhibited by one who has a blood alcohol concentration of 0.05%(Dawson & Reid, 1997). Outside of a laboratory setting, studies examining sleep in the comfort of people’s own homes via self-report surveys have found that, compared with persistently good sleepers persistently poor sleepers experience significantly more daytime difficulies in regards to fatigue, sleepiness, and poor cognition (Alapin et al., 2000).
Sleep is associated with academic performance in school. Sleep deficit has been associated with decreased concentration and attention during class(Orzech et al., 2011). More importantly, the timing of sleep may be particularly relevant to academic performance. In a questionnaire study, Students with higher academic performance reported earlier bedtimes and wake times than students with lower performance(Eliasson et al., 2010). Additionally, under a fixed bedtime could reduce the time available for sleep, making shorter sleep duration one possible explanation for an association between later bedtime and lower GPA.
Taken all together, these studies motivate examining bedtime and sleep duration jointly. The present study used an existing dataset (Onyper et al., 2012) to examine the relationship between average weekday bedtime and GPA among college students.
The present study addressed four research questions:

Is average weekday bedtime associated with GPA?
Does a quadratic term improve the description of the bedtime–GPA association beyond a linear model?
Does the bedtime–GPA association change after accounting for weekday sleep duration?
Is there an indirect statistical association between bedtime and GPA involving weekday sleep duration?

title: Sleep time and GPA
text:
Research Design and Participants
The present study involved a secondary analysis of the SleepStudy dataset, which contains data from 253 college students and identifies Onyper et al. (2012) as its original source. The original data collection included questionnaires about students’ attitudes and habits, cognitive assessments, and sleep diaries maintained over a two-week period. The present analysis focused on three variables: GPA, average weekday bedtime, and average weekday sleep duration. No new participants were recruited, and sleep schedules were not experimentally manipulated.
A complete-case approach was used: students were included if they had nonmissing values on all three variables. The final analytic sample included 253 students. The same sample was used for the correlation, regression, and exploratory mediation analyses to ensure that comparisons across models were based on identical observations.

title: Sleep time and GPA
text:
Measures

Academic Performance
Academic performance was operationalized as GPA, recorded on a 0–4 scale in the dataset. GPA was treated as a continuous outcome variable in all regression analyses.


Weekday Bedtime
Average weekday bedtime was measured using the variable WeekdayBed. Bedtime was recorded in continuous hours, with 24 representing midnight and 25 representing 1:00 a.m. the following day. Higher values therefore indicated later bedtimes. For the quadratic regression, bedtime was centered at midnight by subtracting 24 from the original values. The centered variable and its squared term were included in the model.


Weekday Sleep Duration
Average weekday sleep duration was measured using the variable WeekdaySleep, expressed in hours per night. This variable was included as an additional predictor in the adjusted regression model and as a potential mediator in an exploratory mediation analysis.

title: Sleep time and GPA
text:
Statistical Analysis
Analyses were conducted in Python using pandas, NumPy, SciPy, and statsmodels. Figures were created using Matplotlib and seaborn. Descriptive statistics summarized the distributions of GPA, weekday bedtime, and weekday sleep duration. A scatterplot with a linear regression line and a locally weighted scatterplot smoothing (LOWESS) curve was used to visually examine the form of the bedtime–GPA association.
Pearson’s correlation was calculated to assess the bivariate association between weekday bedtime and GPA. A simple ordinary least squares (OLS) regression was then fitted with GPA as the outcome and weekday bedtime as the predictor. To explore potential curvature, a quadratic model containing midnight-centered bedtime and its squared term was fitted. A nested-model F test examined whether adding the quadratic term improved model fit relative to the linear model.
Diagnostics for the simple linear regression included a residuals-versus-fitted plot to assess linearity and homoscedasticity, a normal Q–Q plot to assess the residual distribution, and an influence plot displaying leverage, externally studentized residuals, and Cook’s distance. These diagnostics were used to identify observations warranting further examination; observations were not excluded on the basis of these diagnostics.
To examine whether the bedtime–GPA association changed after accounting for sleep duration, a multiple regression model included both weekday bedtime and weekday sleep duration as predictors. The bedtime coefficient and explained variance were compared with those from the unadjusted model. For visualization, adjusted predictions were calculated with sleep duration held at its sample mean, and 95% confidence intervals for the predicted mean GPA were displayed.
Finally, an exploratory mediation analysis estimated the indirect association between weekday bedtime and GPA involving weekday sleep duration. Path a was estimated by regressing sleep duration on bedtime. Path b and the adjusted bedtime association, c′, were estimated by regressing GPA on both bedtime and sleep duration. The indirect association was calculated as the product ab.
An approximate 95% Monte Carlo confidence interval for ab was obtained from 100,000 simulated coefficient pairs. Coefficients were sampled independently from normal distributions centered on their OLS estimates, with standard deviations equal to their estimated standard errors. This procedure assumed zero sampling covariance between the estimates of a and b. The 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the simulated products defined the confidence interval. A random seed of 2026 was used for reproducibility.
Regression inference used conventional OLS standard errors. Statistical tests were two-sided with an alpha level of .05, and regression results were reported using unstandardized coefficients and 95% confidence intervals. The quadratic and mediation analyses were treated as exploratory. Because the data were observational, the estimated associations were not interpreted as evidence of causal effects or a causal mediation mechanism.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import statsmodels.api as sm
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf


# 读取数据
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/reisanar/datasets/master/SleepStudy.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(url)

# 保留本次分析需要的变量，删除这些变量中的缺失值
d = df[["GPA", "WeekdayBed", "WeekdaySleep"]].dropna().copy()

display(d.describe())
print("分析样本量：", len(d))


import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from IPython.display import display, Math, Markdown

# 与原分析保持相同的样本选择
d_basic = df[["GPA", "WeekdayBed","WeekdaySleep"]].dropna().copy()
d_basic["bed_c"] = d_basic["WeekdayBed"] - 24

d_sleep = df[
    ["GPA", "WeekdayBed", "WeekdaySleep"]
].dropna().copy()

# 分别命名，避免覆盖之前的 m1、m2
fit_linear = smf.ols(
    "GPA ~ WeekdayBed", data=d_basic
).fit()

fit_quad = smf.ols(
    "GPA ~ bed_c + I(bed_c ** 2)", data=d_basic
).fit()

fit_total = smf.ols(
    "GPA ~ WeekdayBed", data=d_sleep
).fit()

fit_adjusted = smf.ols(
    "GPA ~ WeekdayBed + WeekdaySleep", data=d_sleep
).fit()

fit_a = smf.ols(
    "WeekdaySleep ~ WeekdayBed", data=d_sleep
).fit()


# 自动生成代入系数后的预测方程
def show_equation(title, symbolic, model, outcome, terms):
    display(Markdown(f"**{title}（N = {int(model.nobs)}）**"))
    display(Math(symbolic))

    equation = outcome + f" = {model.params['Intercept']:.4f}"

    for parameter, variable in terms:
        coefficient = model.params[parameter]
        sign = "+" if coefficient >= 0 else "-"
        equation += (
            rf" {sign} {abs(coefficient):.4f}\,{variable}"
        )

    display(Math(equation))

中文报告
散点图显示，工作日就寝时间与 GPA 之间存在轻微的负向趋势，但相同就寝时间下的 GPA 差异较大。LOWESS 平滑线与线性回归线在大部分观测范围内较为接近，未显示明显而稳定的弯曲模式。数据分布两端的观测相对较少，因此这些区域的局部趋势应谨慎解释。
English report
Visual inspection of the scatterplot suggested a slight negative association between weekday bedtime and GPA, with substantial variation in GPA at similar bedtimes. The LOWESS smoother generally followed the linear regression line across most of the observed range, providing little visual evidence of pronounced, systematic curvature. Local trends near the extremes should be interpreted cautiously because observations were relatively sparse in these regions.
结论： 线性模型可以作为初步描述，但就寝时间对学生之间 GPA 差异的解释能力可能较弱。LOWESS 图本身不能确定是否存在显著的非线性关系。

English report
A Pearson correlation indicated a weak negative association between weekday bedtime and GPA, r(251) = −.130, p = .040. Students with later bedtimes tended to report slightly lower GPAs, although the magnitude of the association was small.
结论： 就寝时间与 GPA 的负相关达到 .05 显著性水平，但效应较小，不能据此推断晚睡导致 GPA 降低。

section: 1.2 Research Q2: Does a quadratic term improve the description of the bedtime–GPA association beyond a linear model?
text:
1.2 Research Q2: Does a quadratic term improve the description of the bedtime–GPA association beyond a linear model?


Code
# 使用普通 OLS 标准误
# 确保 m1 是通过 smf.ols(...).fit() 拟合的模型

# 在模型实际使用的就寝时间范围内生成预测点
x = m1.model.exog[:, m1.model.exog_names.index("WeekdayBed")]

prediction_data = pd.DataFrame({
    "WeekdayBed": np.linspace(x.min(), x.max(), 200)
})

pred = m1.get_prediction(prediction_data).summary_frame(alpha=0.05)

# 绘图
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))

ax.scatter(
    x, m1.model.endog,
    alpha=0.4,
    color="steelblue",
    label="Observed GPA"
)

ax.plot(
    prediction_data["WeekdayBed"],
    pred["mean"],
    color="red",
    label="OLS regression line"
)

ax.fill_between(
    prediction_data["WeekdayBed"].to_numpy(),
    pred["mean_ci_lower"].to_numpy(),
    pred["mean_ci_upper"].to_numpy(),
    color="red",
    alpha=0.15,
    label="95% CI (ordinary OLS)"
)

# 横轴显示为时钟时间
ticks = np.arange(np.floor(x.min()), np.ceil(x.max()) + 1)
ax.set_xticks(ticks, [f"{int(t) % 24:02d}:00" for t in ticks])

ax.set_xlabel("Average weekday bedtime")
ax.set_ylabel("GPA")
ax.set_title("Weekday Bedtime and GPA")
ax.legend()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()









中文报告
采用简单线性回归检验工作日就寝时间与 GPA 的关系。模型整体达到统计显著，F(1, 251) = 4.28，p = .040，R² = .017。工作日就寝时间显著负向预测 GPA，b = −0.051，SE = 0.024，t(251) = −2.07，p = .040，95% CI [−0.099, −0.002]。就寝时间每晚 1 小时，预测 GPA 平均降低约 0.051 分。
English report
A simple linear regression examined the association between weekday bedtime and GPA. The overall model was statistically significant, F(1, 251) = 4.28, p = .040, R² = .017. Weekday bedtime negatively predicted GPA, b = −0.051, SE = 0.024, t(251) = −2.07, p = .040, 95% CI [−0.099, −0.002]. Each one-hour later bedtime was associated with an approximately 0.051-point lower predicted GPA.
结论： 普通 OLS 推断下，就寝时间与 GPA 的负关联显著，但模型只解释约 1.7% 的 GPA 方差，解释能力有限。

中文报告
为检验就寝时间与 GPA 之间是否存在二次关系，首先将就寝时间以午夜为中心，再将中心化变量及其平方项纳入回归模型。二次模型整体未达到统计显著，F(2, 250) = 2.27，p = .106，R² = .018。平方项不显著，b = −0.0075，SE = 0.0144，t(250) = −0.52，p = .604，95% CI [−0.0359, 0.0209]。与线性模型相比，增加平方项并未显著改善拟合，ΔF(1, 250) = 0.27，p = .604，ΔR² = .001。
English report
To examine a possible quadratic association, weekday bedtime was centered at midnight, and both the centered term and its square were included in the regression model. The overall quadratic model was not statistically significant, F(2, 250) = 2.27, p = .106, R² = .018. The quadratic term was not significant, b = −0.0075, SE = 0.0144, t(250) = −0.52, p = .604, 95% CI [−0.0359, 0.0209]. Adding the quadratic term did not significantly improve model fit relative to the linear model, ΔF(1, 250) = 0.27, p = .604, ΔR² = .001.
结论： 数据未提供支持二次关系的充分证据，也不足以确定一个使预测 GPA 最高的“最佳就寝时间”。

中文报告
残差与拟合值图未显示明显的系统性曲线模式，LOWESS 平滑线在大部分拟合值范围内接近零。图中也未观察到明显的漏斗形模式，提示线性关系和方差齐性假设未出现突出的视觉违背。不过，部分观测具有较大的负残差。
English report
The residuals-versus-fitted plot showed no pronounced systematic curvature, and the LOWESS smoother remained close to zero across most of the fitted range. No clear funnel-shaped pattern was apparent, suggesting no prominent visual violations of linearity or homoscedasticity. However, several observations had relatively large negative residuals.
结论： 残差图总体支持将线性模型作为初步分析，但图形检查不能证明方差完全相等，也不能排除其他模型问题。

中文报告
正态 Q–Q 图显示，残差在分布中央区域大致接近正态参考线，但在两端出现偏离，尤其是下尾存在较大的负残差。这表明残差分布近似正态，但存在一定的左偏和尾部偏离。
English report
The normal Q–Q plot indicated that residuals approximately followed the normal reference line in the central portion of the distribution. Deviations were evident in the tails, particularly in the lower tail, where several large negative residuals occurred. These findings suggest approximate normality with some negative skewness and tail departures.
结论： 不宜写“残差完全服从正态分布”；更准确的说法是“中央部分近似正态，但尾部存在偏离”。

    ax=axes[2]
)

# 添加学生化残差参考线
axes[2].axhline(
    2, color="red", linestyle="--", label="Residual = ±2"
)
axes[2].axhline(
    -2, color="red", linestyle="--"
)

# 添加杠杆值参考线
n = int(m1.nobs)
p = len(m1.params)  # 包括截距

axes[2].axvline(
    2 * p / n,
    color="orange",
    linestyle="--",
    label="Leverage = 2p/n"
)

axes[2].set_title("Influence Plot")
axes[2].legend()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()


<Figure size 672x480 with 0 Axes>


影响诊断发现，22 个观测的杠杆值超过参考阈值 (2p/n=.0158)，其中 (p=2)，包括截距和一个预测变量。9 个观测的外部学生化残差绝对值超过 2，其中 2 个超过 3。最大 Cook’s distance 为 0.128，没有观测超过 1。部分观测因此值得进一步核查，但这些诊断结果本身不足以支持直接删除观测，也不能确认结果不受影响点影响。
English report
Influence diagnostics identified 22 observations with leverage values exceeding the reference threshold of (2p/n=.0158), where (p=2) included the intercept and one predictor. Nine observations had absolute externally studentized residuals greater than 2, including two greater than 3. The maximum Cook’s distance was 0.128, and no observation exceeded 1. These findings identify cases warranting further examination but do not, by themselves, justify excluding observations or establish that the results are insensitive to influential cases.
结论： 存在需要关注的观测。应先核查数据是否有误；如需评价结果稳定性，可以补充敏感性分析，而不是仅根据气泡大小删除学生。

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# 生成连续的入睡时间，用来画回归线
bed_grid = np.linspace(
    d_sleep["WeekdayBed"].min(),
    d_sleep["WeekdayBed"].max(),
    200
)

# 模型 2：将睡眠时长固定在样本平均值
mean_sleep = d_sleep["WeekdaySleep"].mean()

prediction_data = pd.DataFrame({
    "WeekdayBed": bed_grid,
    "WeekdaySleep": mean_sleep
})

# 两个模型的预测值及 95% 置信区间
pred1 = m1.get_prediction(prediction_data).summary_frame(alpha=0.05)
pred2 = m2.get_prediction(prediction_data).summary_frame(alpha=0.05)

    d_sleep["WeekdayBed"],
    d_sleep["GPA"],
    color="gray",
    alpha=0.25,
    s=25,
    label="Observed data"
)

# 模型 1：未控制睡眠时长
ax.plot(
    bed_grid,
    pred1["mean"].to_numpy(),
    color="#2878B5",
    linewidth=2.5,
    label="Model 1: Unadjusted"
)

    bed_grid,
    pred1["mean_ci_lower"].to_numpy(),
    pred1["mean_ci_upper"].to_numpy(),

)

# 模型 2：控制睡眠时长
ax.plot(
    bed_grid,
    pred2["mean"].to_numpy(),
    color="#D95319",
    linewidth=2.5,
    linestyle="--",
    label="Model 2: Adjusted for sleep duration"
)

)

    xlabel="Weekday bedtime (original coding)",

    transform=ax.transAxes,

中文报告
使用相同的 253 个完整观测，比较未控制和控制工作日睡眠时长的回归模型。加入睡眠时长后，模型整体显著，F(2, 250) = 6.85，p = .001，R² = .052，较未调整模型增加约 .035 的解释方差。控制睡眠时长后，较晚就寝仍与较低 GPA 相关，且系数绝对值由 0.051 增大至 0.102，b = −0.102，SE = 0.029，t(250) = −3.47，p < .001，95% CI [−0.160, −0.044]。此外，控制就寝时间后，较长睡眠时长也与较低 GPA 相关，b = −0.079，SE = 0.026，t(250) = −3.04，p = .003，95% CI [−0.130, −0.028]。
比较图将睡眠时长固定为样本均值 7.87 小时，以展示调整后的预测 GPA；橙色回归线表示这一固定睡眠时长下的预测关系。
English report
Unadjusted and adjusted regression models were compared using the same 253 complete observations. After weekday sleep duration was added, the overall model was significant, F(2, 250) = 6.85, p = .001, R² = .052, representing an increase of approximately .035 in explained variance. Controlling for sleep duration, later bedtime remained associated with lower GPA, and the coefficient increased in absolute magnitude from 0.051 to 0.102, b = −0.102, SE = 0.029, t(250) = −3.47, p < .001, 95% CI [−0.160, −0.044]. Controlling for bedtime, longer sleep duration was also associated with lower GPA, b = −0.079, SE = 0.026, t(250) = −3.04, p = .003, 95% CI [−0.130, −0.028].
For visualization, sleep duration was held at its sample mean of 7.87 hours. The orange regression line therefore represents the adjusted association at that fixed sleep duration.

title: Sleep time and GPA
section: 1.4 Research Q4:Is there an indirect statistical association between bedtime and GPA involving weekday sleep duration?
text:
1.4 Research Q4:Is there an indirect statistical association between bedtime and GPA involving weekday sleep duration?


Code
import numpy as np
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# 1. 两个模型使用相同的完整观测
d_med = df[
    ["WeekdayBed", "WeekdaySleep", "GPA"]
].dropna().copy()

# 2. 路径 a：就寝时间 → 睡眠时长
model_a = smf.ols(
    "WeekdaySleep ~ WeekdayBed",
    data=d_med
).fit()

# 路径 b 和 c'：同时预测 GPA
model_b = smf.ols(
    "GPA ~ WeekdayBed + WeekdaySleep",
    data=d_med
).fit()

# 3. 提取系数与普通 OLS 标准误
a = model_a.params["WeekdayBed"]
se_a = model_a.bse["WeekdayBed"]

b = model_b.params["WeekdaySleep"]
se_b = model_b.bse["WeekdaySleep"]

c_prime = model_b.params["WeekdayBed"]

# 4. Monte Carlo：模拟系数的抽样分布
rng = np.random.default_rng(2026)
n_sim = 100_000

# 基础方法：近似假设 a、b 的抽样协方差为 0
a_sim = rng.normal(a, se_a, n_sim)
b_sim = rng.normal(b, se_b, n_sim)

indirect_sim = a_sim * b_sim

# 5. 间接关联及其 95% Monte Carlo 置信区间
indirect = a * b
ci_low, ci_high = np.quantile(indirect_sim, [0.025, 0.975])

print(f"N = {len(d_med)}")
print(f"a = {a:.4f}")
print(f"b = {b:.4f}")
print(f"c' = {c_prime:.4f}")
print(f"Indirect association (a × b) = {indirect:.4f}")
print(f"95% Monte Carlo CI = [{ci_low:.4f}, {ci_high:.4f}]")

# 6. 展示模拟得到的间接关联分布
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))

ax.hist(
    indirect_sim,
    bins=60,
    color="steelblue",
    edgecolor="white"
)

ax.axvline(0, color="black", linestyle="--", label="Zero")
ax.axvline(ci_low, color="red", linestyle="--", label="95% CI limits")
ax.axvline(ci_high, color="red", linestyle="--")

ax.set_xlabel("Simulated indirect association (a × b)")
ax.set_ylabel("Frequency")
ax.set_title("Monte Carlo Distribution of the Indirect Association")
ax.legend()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# 4. 控制睡眠时长：也是中介分析中的 b 和 c′ 方程
show_equation(
    "4. 控制睡眠时长：路径 b 和 c′",
    r"\mathrm{GPA}_i=\nu_0"
    r"+c'\mathrm{WeekdayBed}_i"
    r"+b\,\mathrm{WeekdaySleep}_i+\varepsilon_{Y,i}",
    fit_adjusted,
    r"\widehat{\mathrm{GPA}}_i",
    [
        ("WeekdayBed", r"\mathrm{WeekdayBed}_i"),
        ("WeekdaySleep", r"\mathrm{WeekdaySleep}_i")
    ]
)

# 5. 中介分析中的路径 a
show_equation(
    "5. 就寝时间预测睡眠时长：路径 a",
    r"\mathrm{WeekdaySleep}_i=\mu_0"
    r"+a\,\mathrm{WeekdayBed}_i+\varepsilon_{M,i}",
    fit_a,
    r"\widehat{\mathrm{WeekdaySleep}}_i",
    [("WeekdayBed", r"\mathrm{WeekdayBed}_i")]
)

# 6. 代入实际系数，显示关联分解
a_hat = fit_a.params["WeekdayBed"]
b_hat = fit_adjusted.params["WeekdaySleep"]
c_hat = fit_total.params["WeekdayBed"]
cp_hat = fit_adjusted.params["WeekdayBed"]
ab_hat = a_hat * b_hat

display(Markdown("**6. 间接关联与总关联分解**"))

display(Math(
    rf"\hat a\hat b"
    rf"=({a_hat:.4f})\times({b_hat:.4f})"
    rf"={ab_hat:.4f}"

a = -0.6460
b = -0.0791
c' = -0.1018
Indirect association (a × b) = 0.0511
95% Monte Carlo CI = [0.0179, 0.0866]









4. 控制睡眠时长：路径 b 和 c′（N = 253）


\(\displaystyle \mathrm{GPA}_i=\nu_0+c'\mathrm{WeekdayBed}_i+b\,\mathrm{WeekdaySleep}_i+\varepsilon_{Y,i}\)


\(\displaystyle \widehat{\mathrm{GPA}}_i = 6.3951 - 0.1018\,\mathrm{WeekdayBed}_i - 0.0791\,\mathrm{WeekdaySleep}_i\)


5. 就寝时间预测睡眠时长：路径 a（N = 253）


\(\displaystyle \mathrm{WeekdaySleep}_i=\mu_0+a\,\mathrm{WeekdayBed}_i+\varepsilon_{M,i}\)


\(\displaystyle \widehat{\mathrm{WeekdaySleep}}_i = 23.9186 - 0.6460\,\mathrm{WeekdayBed}_i\)


6. 间接关联与总关联分解


\(\displaystyle \hat a\hat b=(-0.6460)\times(-0.0791)=0.0511\)


\(\displaystyle \hat c=\hat c'+\hat a\hat b=(-0.1018)+(0.0511)=-0.0507\)


中文报告
探索性中介分析检验了工作日睡眠时长所对应的间接关联。较晚就寝与较短睡眠时长显著相关，路径 (a=-0.646)，SE = 0.058，t(251) = −11.04，p < .001，95% CI [−0.761, −0.531]。控制就寝时间后，睡眠时长与 GPA 呈负关联，路径 (b=-0.079)，SE = 0.026，t(250) = −3.04，p = .003，95% CI [−0.130, −0.028]。
估计间接关联为 (ab=0.051)。基于 100,000 次 Monte Carlo 模拟，95% CI 为 [0.018, 0.087]，不包含零。直接关联为 (c’=-0.102)，总关联为 (c=-0.051)。间接关联与直接关联方向相反，呈现与不一致中介或抑制模式相符的统计结果。由于数据为观察性数据，该分析不能确立因果中介机制。
English report
An exploratory mediation analysis examined the indirect association involving weekday sleep duration. Later bedtime was significantly associated with shorter sleep duration, path (a=-0.646), SE = 0.058, t(251) = −11.04, p < .001, 95% CI [−0.761, −0.531]. Controlling for bedtime, sleep duration was negatively associated with GPA, path (b=-0.079), SE = 0.026, t(250) = −3.04, p = .003, 95% CI [−0.130, −0.028].
The estimated indirect association was (ab=0.051). A 95% Monte Carlo confidence interval based on 100,000 simulations excluded zero, [0.018, 0.087]. The direct association was (c’=-0.102), whereas the total association was (c=-0.051). The opposing signs of the indirect and direct associations were consistent with an inconsistent mediation or suppression pattern. Because the data were observational, these findings do not establish a causal mediation mechanism.
